body:
On Julia 1.13, we have

```julia
julia> reduce(vcat, [1])
1-element Vector{Int64}:
 1
```

and on Julia 1.12, we have

```julia-repl
julia> reduce(vcat, [1])
1
```

In EKP, we have

```julia
mean(pd::ParameterDistribution) = reduce(vcat, mean.(pd.distribution))
```

at https://github.com/CliMA/EnsembleKalmanProcesses.jl/blob/8051608c39236b90903c2d55e43576c778df1c84/src/ParameterDistributions.jl#L754.

This line above returns a vector of a single value on Julia v1.13 and a single value on Julia v1.12. This difference causes lines like

```julia
init_params = ndims(prior) > 1 ? mean(prior) : [mean(prior)]
```

to return an expression of the form `[[1.0]]` if the mean is 1.0. This breaks other code of CES. This is fixed by using `vcat(mean(prior))` which always return a vector.

This PR also makes a new release, so that it can be used in ClimaLand.

related: https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/issues/1959

I asked a LLM to make the code change for this PR.
title: Fix for Julia v1.13
